the college is the Guardian for the majority of the students under 18 and so should they fall ill and need to be taken to Hospital at any time the Warden does this. He also stays in the hospital until s/he has been seen by medical staff which can be most of the night depending on the case. Indeed any kind of difficulty including ones which require counselling is attended to. This service will continue as at present. 
Although, our students who are over 18 do not require a Guardian nonetheless they need the same services should they fall ill or have an accident. With the increasing numbers of students and the growing number of happily relative minor incidents which required Hospital visits this year the college has felt the impact on our services and consequently staffing. With an increase in staff commitments there has been a cost implication. 
So from September 2013 onwards there will be a charge of £500.00 per annum for students over 18 year in order to provide this service. 
Should a student decline this option they will need to make their own arrangements; provide their own designated person or Guardian who would undertake to provide them with a comparable assistance. However, in any case, rest assured the college will discharge its duty of care to all its students.

The halls of residence are self catering only although lunch is available at the college. Alternatively, host families provide breakfast and dinner during the week and all meals at the weekend. Halls of residence do require maturity and independence as students will need to shop, cook and clean for themselves.

The halls of residence rooms are all single. Students can live in either a house which has three bedrooms or a flat which has two bedrooms. Every room is ensuite. Each house and flat has their own kitchen. There is a common area with a pool table, tv etc. The halls are 8 miles from the college. There is a shuttle for the first month from the halls. The students will be given a bus pass which will allow them to travel by bus after the first month. The busses run every ten minutes and it is very easy. Halls are all self catering.

Students can move into the halls from Saturday the 28th August. Students need to be at college on the 1st of September for induction.

Host family

[28 Jan 2014]
You have chosen to stay with a homestay provider as a paying guest.  You will usually be the only student from your country in the homestay.  This is a valuable opportunity to experience life in a ‘typical’ household, and to hear and speak English outside the classroom.

All our our homestay providers have agreed to abide by the Homestay Code of Practice.  This means that your host will promise:

•	To encourage you to speak English as much as possible in the home
•	To encourage you to feel at home and to treat you as a member of the household rather than a paying guest
•	Not to host another student of the same native language as you at the same time (unless by special agreement with both of you)
•	To provide a clean and comfortable room as recommended by the British Council
•	To provide a home environment you can carry on your English studies properly including use of internet/wireless if they have this facility
•	To provide you with a balanced and appropriate diet
•	To show due concern for your welfare, safety and security during your stay
•	For protection of all members of the household, we ask that doors remain open when alone in a room with a student.
•	To give you reasonable and regular access to bathroom and laundry facilities (some families will do your laundry for you)
•	To communicate regularly with the college and so be in a position to help resolve any problems you may encounter during your stay
•	To respect your different cultural background and be sensitive to your particular needs

The fees for homestay accommodation will be £130 per week for half board (breakfast and evening meal Monday to Friday, three meals Saturday and Sunday) although you may choose to pay for full board only and this can be agreed with your homestay family. If you pay the homestay fees for the year, then the college will issue a cheque to the host family each term.  However, you may prefer to pay the family yourself every four weeks.  There will be a retainer fee payable of £30 per week, payable in advance, when you return home for the holidays.

Some of the homestay families will have children who attend the college, and in other families you will be the youngest member of the household.

If you have any worries about your homestay accommodation you can discuss them with the Admissions Manager at the college.  The relationship with past students and homestay families has been very successful in the past and we are sure you will soon settle in and be made to feel very welcome.

- The UK govt is making reforms to A-level programmes, effect from Sep 2015 
- Currently, students in Y12 (typically take 4 x AS-levels) --> Y13 (3 x  A-levels) will continue
- Main change: the AS-level grade will no longer contribute towards the overall A-level grade, which currently the AS-level grade shall contribute towards the overall A-level result
(But students will receive a separate AS qualification in addition to their final A-level qualification)


What does this mean for international students at West Buckland School?

- For those international students studying for a limited period of up to one year in Year 12, our Sixth Form curriculum will be very similar to the current arrangements.  
- Students will still normally be expected to take four AS-level subjects in addition to studying English as a Second Language (ESL).  
- Students will receive a full programme of teaching and learning right through to midway into the Summer Term before sitting the AS examinations in May/June.

- For students undertaking the full two year A-level programme and progressing into Year 13, they will continue to typically study three A-level subjects plus ESL.
